subject: Urgent: p95 error-rate spike and throughput degradation on Argosy Bio private cluster
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@argosybio.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Argosy DevOps <devops@argosybio.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden spike in 500s and throughput drop on our private cluster

Marcus / Redwood team —

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95 latencies and a rise in 500 responses from our private VPC deployment this morning (~06:00 UTC). Throughput (req/s) dropped by ~35% across the board. This is impacting our downstream ingestion pipelines and a scheduled nightly job failed as a result.

Quick facts:
- Region: us-west-2 (your private VPC deployment)
- First observed: 2027-02-20 06:02 UTC
- Error rate: 500s increased from ~0.2% baseline to ~6% p95 window
- P95 latency: jumped from ~210ms to ~1.1s for generation endpoints

I attached a screenshot of the dashboard and the KV stats CSV exported from our side. We are in a production run and need immediate help — could you triage and propose short-term mitigation? If we need to fall back to a hosted variant for a brief window, we need guidance and a plan.

Thank you,
Lena Ortiz
Platform Lead, Argosy Bio
lena.ortiz@argosybio.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@argosybio.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in 500s and throughput drop on our private cluster

Thanks for flagging, Lena — we see the alerts in our control plane as well. I'm opening an incident and will coordinate triage. Immediate asks from my side:

1) Can you confirm whether any config changes or model rollbacks were applied to the private cluster in the last 24 hours?
2) Please keep the exported logs (client-side traces) available; we've requested devops attach them to the ticket.

We will:
- Engage SRE to capture kernel/driver metrics and KV cache hit rates
- Evaluate whether batching parameters or the quantized variant routing changed unexpectedly
- Prepare a short mitigation (routing to a compatible hosted model variant with transparent fallbacks) if we can't restore within 45 minutes

Looping in: Olga (SRE) for infra triage, Neha (Support) for customer comms and a possible rollback plan, and Priyom (Solutions Eng) for workload/throughput tuning.

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, priyom.das@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: lena.ortiz@argosybio.com, devops@argosybio.com
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in 500s and throughput drop on our private cluster

Triage update (initial):

What I see so far from control plane + Argosy-provided kvstats:
- KV cache miss rate jumped from ~12% to ~48% starting 06:00 UTC.
- GPU utilization is uneven across the pool; a set of nodes shows sustained high GPU mem pressure and intermittent OOM throttling in the tracer logs.
- There are occasional failed kernel calls reported in the instance syslogs (attached excerpt).

Hypothesis: a model variant or tokenization edge-case caused KV cache churn + uneven batching leading to OOMs on some nodes, cascading into 500s and throughput reduction.

Immediate steps taken:
- Isolated the affected GPU subset and marked them for prioritized log collection.
- Increased min-batch timeout to reduce tiny-batch pressure (incremental change).
- Disabled a non-essential third-party pre-processing hook that correlated with requests in the attached sample.

Attachments: argosy-kvstats-20270220.csv, infra-syslog-excerpt.txt

Next actions I recommend:
1) Short-term mitigation: route a % of traffic to a compatible hosted quantized variant (we can do 20-40% traffic shift) while we drain and reprovision the affected nodes. This buys time and reduces error-rate exposure.
2) Mid-term: run a KV-cache consistency job and re-evaluate batching strategy; consider pinning to a variant with a smaller KV footprint.
3) Exec sync if Argosy wants to evaluate credit/compensation — we should be ready for a customer exec call.

I'll keep collecting traces, will update in 20–30 minutes.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@argosy.bio>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in 500s and throughput drop on our private cluster

Hi Lena — quick comms plan and proposed actions:

1) Short window mitigation (recommended):
   - Shift 30% of traffic to a hosted Quantized-A variant compatible with your model. Estimated time to switch: 10–15 minutes once you approve.
   - We will keep request routing sticky for the remaining 70% to preserve cache locality.
2) If you prefer no routing change, we can perform a rolling drain of the affected nodes and provision replacements; ETA ~60–90 minutes but with higher risk of transient errors during drains.
3) I'll schedule an exec bridge if Argosy leadership wants an immediate triage — Marcus, please confirm if we should loop in Sales leadership for possible credit conversation.

Customer-facing note you can use for internal stakeholders:
"Redwood has identified a KV-cache churn and node-level memory pressure as the root cause of returning 500 errors. We are routing a portion of your traffic to a compatible hosted model and replacing affected nodes to restore full throughput. More details to follow after logs and traces are analyzed."

Attachments: runbook-redwood-v2.pdf (relevant runbook excerpt).

Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
From: Tom Harper <tom.harper@argosybio.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@argosybio.com>, priyom.das@argosybio.com
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 17:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in 500s and throughput drop on our private cluster

Team —

Thanks for the quick responses overnight. Impact summary from our side:
- Two scheduled ETL windows missed; downstream SLA breached for 6 hours.
- One downstream customer reported missed alerts.
- Financial exposure estimated at ~$18k in processing delays and manual remediation time.

We want to escalate this to a formal post-incident review. Please include:
- A timeline of events with root-cause analysis (including when the KV cache churn started and why batching changes didn’t prevent OOMs).
- The list of nodes affected and kernel/log excerpts.
- Proposed permanent mitigations and an expected timeline for deployment.

We also request an exec sync with Redwood CTO or VP of SRE this week to review compensation and long-term safeguards.

Tom Harper
VP, Infrastructure — Argosy Bio
Tom.Harper@argosybio.com
